extracted.intended_audience: school, college, and university administrators and Title IX personnel (Coordinators, investigators, decision‑makers), and institutional legal counsel
extracted.subtask_description: Federal Department of Education final‑rule guidance describing the standardized grievance process and procedural requirements recipients (K–12 and postsecondary institutions receiving federal funds) must adopt for handling formal complaints of sexual harassment under Title IX.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fundamental due process principles
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedural due process requires at minimum notice and a meaningful opportunity to be heard; due process is flexible and must be tailored to the 'particular situation.' The fundamental requirement is the opportunity to be heard 'at a meaningful time and in a meaningful manner.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department recognizes courts have not defined exactly which procedures are constitutionally required in Title IX adjudications, but §106.45 is designed to be consistent with constitutional due process by ensuring notice and meaningful opportunities to be heard for complainants and respondents. Due process protections may differ by context (e.g., elementary/secondary vs. postsecondary) and are intended to promote fair, accurate outcomes and reduce sex‑based bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 106.45(a) — acknowledgment of potential sex discrimination
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 106.45(a) acknowledges that a recipient's treatment of a complainant or a respondent could constitute sex discrimination prohibited under Title IX.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provision frames the grievance process within Title IX's nondiscrimination mandate and signals that institutional responses can themselves be discriminatory and must therefore follow the prescribed grievance framework.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 106.45(b)(1)(i)-(x) — core grievance process requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must adopt a grievance process that treats complainants and respondents equitably, objectively evaluates all relevant evidence, ensures Title IX personnel are free from conflicts and trained impartially, presumes respondents not responsible until the process concludes, includes reasonably prompt timeframes, informs parties of critical procedural information (including remedies, sanctions, standard of evidence, appeal procedures, and supportive measures), and protects legally recognized privileges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific elements listed include: (i) equitable treatment and remedies/sanctions balance; (ii) objective evaluation of inculpatory and exculpatory evidence and parity in rules adopted by the recipient; (iii) Title IX Coordinators, investigators, decision‑makers, and informal resolution facilitators must be free from conflicts of interest and bias and trained to serve impartially; (iv) presumption of non‑responsibility for respondents until a determination; (v) reasonably prompt timeframes (recipient may set 'reasonably prompt' timeframes); (vi) parties must be informed of range of remedies/disciplinary sanctions, the standard of evidence used (either preponderance or clear and convincing), the recipient's appeal procedures, and supportive measures available; (vii) legally recognized privileges are protected. The Department explains these requirements are rooted in notice and meaningful hearing principles to promote fairness and accuracy and to limit sex‑based bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 106.45(b)(2) — written notice of allegations and advisor choice
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must provide written notice of the allegations to both parties and inform them of the right to select an advisor of their choice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Written notice must be sufficiently detailed to permit parties to prepare for an initial interview and must be sent 'upon receipt of a formal complaint.' The final rule makes written notice mandatory for both parties (unlike prior guidance which was only advisory or directed to the respondent).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sections 106.45(b)(3)-(b)(4) — investigation, dismissal, notification, consolidation
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients are required to investigate formal complaints, specify when a formal complaint is subject to mandatory or discretionary dismissal, notify parties of any dismissal, and may consolidate formal complaints when allegations arise out of the same facts or circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rule clarifies obligations to investigate and to give notice when complaints or allegations are dismissed; discretionary consolidation is permitted when appropriate (same facts/circumstances). The Department emphasizes that notice of dismissal and ability to appeal are important for accuracy and fairness even if not constitutionally required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 106.45(b)(5)(i)-(vii) — investigation procedures and parties' rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigations must keep the burden of proof and gathering evidence on the recipient while protecting a party's right to consent to use of their treatment records; provide parties equal opportunity to present witnesses and inculpatory/exculpatory evidence; not restrict parties from discussing allegations or gathering evidence; allow equal opportunity to select an advisor; give written notice when a party's participation is invited or expected; provide both parties equal opportunity to review and respond to evidence; and send both parties the investigative report summarizing relevant evidence before a determination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key protections include: recipient retains responsibility for investigation (burden on recipient), treatment/medical/psychological records cannot be used without voluntary written consent of the party, both parties must receive copies of evidence 'directly related to the allegations,' and must receive the investigative report prior to any determination. The Department frames these requirements as building on prior guidance and as necessary to reach accurate, reliable determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 106.45(b)(6) — hearing and cross‑examination rules (postsecondary vs. K–12)
rubrics_metrics.description: Postsecondary institutions must hold a live hearing with cross‑examination conducted by the parties' advisors; elementary and secondary schools (and other non‑postsecondary recipients) are not required to hold live hearings but must give parties equal opportunity to submit written questions for other parties and witnesses to answer before a determination is reached.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provision distinguishes postsecondary institutions (mandatory live hearings and advisor‑conducted cross‑examination) from K–12 or other recipients (optional hearings with equivalent written question procedures). The Department notes prior guidance was silent or inconsistent on hearings and cross‑examination; §106.45 clarifies and mandates advisor‑conducted cross‑examination at postsecondary hearings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 106.45(b)(7) — decision‑maker independence, standard of evidence, and written determination
rubrics_metrics.description: A decision‑maker who is not the Title IX Coordinator or the investigator must reach the determination regarding responsibility, applying the standard of evidence selected by the recipient (preponderance of the evidence or clear and convincing), and the recipient must simultaneously send both parties a written determination explaining the reasons for the outcome.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rule requires separation of investigative and adjudicatory functions, permits recipients to choose between two evidence standards (but requires the chosen standard be applied to all formal complaints), and mandates timely, reasoned written determinations to both parties at the same time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 106.45(b)(8) — equal appeals rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must offer appeals equally to both parties on grounds that procedural deficiencies, newly discovered evidence, or bias or conflict of interest affected the outcome.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appeals must be available to both complainants and respondents and may be based on specified grounds; this is intended to provide a mechanism to correct errors or address unfairness that affected the original outcome.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 106.45(b)(9) — parameters for informal resolution
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients may offer and facilitate informal resolution processes (e.g., mediation) only with the voluntary, written consent of both parties, and informal resolution may not be used to resolve allegations that an employee sexually harassed a student.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The final rule allows informal resolution where both parties agree in writing, but prohibits informal resolution for employee‑student harassment. This departs from earlier guidance that discouraged mediation for sexual assault; the Department retains limits to protect vulnerable parties and to avoid inappropriate use of informal processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 106.45(b)(10) — records retention and training transparency
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must maintain records and documentation concerning sexual harassment reports, formal complaints, investigations, and adjudications, and must publish materials used for training Title IX Coordinators, investigators, decision‑makers, and informal resolution facilitators on their website or make them available upon request to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recordkeeping and public availability of training materials are intended to promote accountability, transparency, and consistent implementation of procedures across recipients.
